newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng Bank denies China seeks stake.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank denies China seeks stake.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd said it welcomed the participation of Chinese companies in Hong Kong's banking sector but dismissed speculation that a mainland company could buy a stake in the HSBC Holdings Plc unit.
"This comes as a surprise to me," vice chairman and chief executive Alexander Au said on Wednesday of the market rumours.
"I am not aware of any approach...as far as I know, there is no intention on the part of HongKong Bank (HSBC) to divest or sell holdings, it's never been discussed," he told a seminar.

Shares in Hang Seng Bank Ltd soared last week along with other banking stocks as investors sought out possible targets for acquisition by mainland companies. The stock closed down HK$0.50 at HK$103.00 on Wednesday.

Although speculation of an immiment mainland stake in Hang Seng Bank or parent HSBC have surfaced before, both political and commercial arguments for such a move were weak, Merrill Lynch banking analyst Keith Irving said in a recent report.
China could be eyeing a stake in the bank sector and dismantle another perceived British monopoly, but the People's Republic of China already had corporate sovereignty, Irving said.
"I would take encouragement from the fact that they are prepared to invest in Hong Kong and clearly see prospects in Hong Kong," said Au.

"Whether that will enhance earnings prospects it's very difficult to say, for example if it has connections in China which it can usefully channel to Hong Kong, to banks in Hong Kong, obviously that would be helpful," he said.
The Bank of China has about 25 percent of the local market with about 360 branches in the territory, the same as Hang Seng Bank and Hongkong Bank combined, said Irving.
Increased mainland access for banks may not affect earnings over the next few years, given the restrictions which still apply in China and the difficulty of making a credit assessment, he said.
